I’m よしたか (Yoshitaka) the developer of TopazChat audio/video streaming service. Thank you for posting this canny. I also want TopazChat to be whitelisted by VRChat.

We’ve been providing our service since August 2019 for free. Thankfully we have many VRChat users and patrons to keep continuing our service.

Of cause our service don’t collect the sensitive information of our users. The IP addresses are only used to provide our service (responding incoming packets), and logs to solving technical problems, no exposure to any third-party.

Our TopazChat is trusted by many VRChat communities for 4 years long, and supporting many performers by our ultra low latency & high quality audio/video streaming.

Please add following domains to whitelist:

- topaz.chat for public usage

- *.topaz.chat subdomains for special event purposes.

If you require more information, please email me at tyounan.moti@gmail.com or DM @TyounanMOTI at X (Twitter)

@{5baf6139b49f620eba95cdfa|full_name}: As per as my knowledge of recently added trust domain, all domain owners be business partner and registered business.

So best bet to archive this be, make partnership agreement with VRChat and ask them to add those domain as per as you required.

(Basically, this is part of corporate relationship department matter)

This request has been partially implemented it seems?

https://creators.vrchat.com/worlds/udon/video-players/www-whitelist/#allowlisted-services

shows that only ciel.topaz.chat is permitted. Unsure if this domain is specific to a particular event or partner.

details:
VRChat has a whitelisting system for video player and livestream hosts, shown here: https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/www-whitelist
but the whitelist itself has not been updated for some time.
Unfortunately one of the most widely used VRChat streaming services is still not on the whitelist: TopazChat ( `*.topaz.chat` )
See here for the absurdly complex instructions that the JP community is forced to do.
https://twitter.com/Coquelicots_WoT/status/1581208227382906880
When users do this, they are opening themselves up for all worlds, due to the fact that whitelists were rushed in 2 years ago and never updated.
Furthermore, *official events* and unofficial events often ask participants to enable Allow Untrusted URLs. VRChat should work with event planners to resolve this in the whitelist so once again you don't have users opening themselves up to privacy leaks.
Regards,
Lyuma
title: Add TopazChat to whitelist
